summary:
We developed a game for children who do not have the ability to access education to the fullest extent possible but are nevertheless passionate about STEM and determined to achieve their goals.

Colony Frontier is a game designed by Team ACG, which consists of five developers from Auckland, New Zealand, who believe in humanity. We think there are thousands of Einsteins out there, thousands of Elon Musks.

And so, we made Colony Frontier, an open-source game with over [complete this part]. It's not purely for this competition; it's to give everyone a chance at space.

We task whoever experiences the game with launching a rocket to a precise altitude, using real formulas that apply to actual liftoff, and then surviving challenges they will actually face on a real moon base.

It features a live Google Translate API, so no one gets left out, and a simple way of use, so everyone can use it. No fancy terminology, no coding experience required, and a very user-friendly and vivid UI.
details:
There are many people smarter than us. We all know that. But let's think deeper. What about those who are smarter than us but have fewer resources? Take Ramanujan, for example. Many mathematical breakthroughs would have been impossible without his genius. Although being born in a poor Indian village, he had limited opportunities despite belonging to the Brahmin caste, a traditionally high-status social group. His father worked three jobs as a bookkeeper, clerk, and accountant, earning very little. Ramanujan despised school, as his teachers forced him to work at the same level as his peers, despite being far ahead of them. It was not until he was 25 that his work finally gained recognition overseas. Now, imagine what he could have achieved had he possessed the resources to publish and pursue his work in his own country.

Colony Frontier works by putting you in a hypothetical moon base and giving you problem to fix. Living in a moon base isn't sunshine and rainbows. You will spend around one moon day, which is about 14 earth days or a Fortnite in simplified terms. You will struggle with energy, with food, with oxygen etc. This should be taught to children at a young age-How to problem solve while in space. We have dedicated most of the project to children in third world countries who simply cannot access good technology or education. This is the reason it runs purely on the web. Anyone can play it with a laptop that can connect to the internet. It also has a live google translation API so everyone can read it. Colony frontier lets everyone reach for the stars. It is simply our motto.
dataRefs: How can children prepare to be an astronaut
